name: Mother St. James Memorial Building, Beryl Ivey Library and Academic Pavilion
summary: Tall pale fins and green spandrel panels define the north academic block, joined to the adjacent wings by a lower stone entrance. Silver siding, charcoal panels, and large projecting glass bays clad the south pavilion.

evidence.note: North approach. Narrow vertical window stacks alternate with projecting pale fins. The east entrance roof lies below the finned block.
Front steps, green-blue fascia, glass doors and rough stone. The HDR connector photograph shows two main rows of windows. Pale fin and green spandrel colours were sampled there.

Architect photographs show the two-storey south addition, corrugated silver cladding, projecting dark metal, light concrete base, large glazed bays and glazed connector. Sunlit piers, green spandrels and pavilion base were sampled from the material and connector views.
Map locates Beryl Ivey Library on the west, the Academic Pavilion on the south and accessible entrances.

City of London 2025 orthophoto. Distinct roofs over five linked ranges. Mechanical plant sits in the middle of the southern arm. A separate white-roofed projection lies southeast of the older academic block.
Inventory P50 9.79 m, P90 13.99 m, maximum 15.45 m. Tall central roof is near 14 m, western library and eastern range near 10–11 m, southeast projection near 7 m. South-wing returns vary strongly.
The north wall stone is in deep shade in the facilities photo. Its daylight colour is estimated by comparing adjacent light piers in the street and architect photographs.

Two tall rows of occupied windows lie above a short basement light strip. Horizontal sash divisions form several smaller tiers within each row. The teal entrance fascia runs below the taller finned volume.
Mother St James shows a projecting upper storey around a recessed plant well and a narrow separately roofed link in orthophoto imagery.

notes: The north fin pattern and pavilion cladding are documented, and bay counts elsewhere are estimated. Upper-storey metal volumes project beyond the concrete ground walls. The glazed connector and cladding transitions occur within single inventory wall segments.
